course.title: Entrepreneurship and Business Creation
course.description: From spotting problems worth solving to testing ideas, planning, financing and launching a small enterprise. Practical path from first idea to early growth.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.1: Problems worth solving
lessons.description: Find painful, frequent problems people will pay to reduce.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

List real problems you observe and score them for pain, frequency and willingness to pay.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.2: Understanding customers and markets
lessons.description: Who has the problem and how they solve it today.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Describe a target customer and their current alternatives.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.3: Testing an idea cheaply
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Design a low-cost test that would change your mind about the idea.

lessons.title: Module 1 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 1 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: A strong opportunity often combines:
Rare pain and no willingness to pay
*Meaningful pain, frequency, and willingness to pay
Only your personal preference
Zero competition forever
explain: Pain + frequency + payment intent.
level: 1

Q: Understanding current alternatives matters because:
Customers have no alternatives
*Your offer must be better enough on dimensions they care about
Alternatives are illegal
Only price matters
explain: Switching requires superiority on valued dimensions.
level: 1

Q: A cheap test should:
Require full product build first
*Produce evidence that increases or decreases confidence in the idea
Only confirm your bias
Cost as much as a full launch
explain: Learning per shilling.
level: 1

Q: Talking to potential customers early helps:
Waste time
*Reveal real needs and language they use
Replace all testing
Guarantee success
explain: Customer language and needs.
level: 1

Q: “Build it and they will come” is risky because:
It is always true
*It skips validation of demand
Customers never change
Marketing is free
explain: Demand validation first.
level: 2

Q: Scoring problems helps you:
Treat all ideas as equal
*Compare and prioritise which to pursue first
Avoid all research
Focus only on easy problems
explain: Prioritisation.
level: 2

Q: A target customer description should include:
Everyone in the country
*Specific characteristics of people who feel the problem most acutely
Only age
Only income
explain: Specificity focuses learning.
level: 1

Q: Willingness to pay can be explored by:
Assuming it is high
*Asking about current spend and testing real offers or pre-orders carefully
Ignoring money entirely
Only surveying friends
explain: Behaviour beats hypotheticals.
level: 2

Q: An experiment that cannot change your mind is:
Useful science
*Not a real test
Required by investors
The best design
explain: Falsifiability matters.
level: 2

Q: The goal of early opportunity work is:
Perfect business plans
*Reduce uncertainty about problem, customer and demand before heavy spend
Immediate scale
Avoiding all contact with customers
explain: De-risk early.
level: 1

lessons.title: Lesson 2.1: Value for customers
lessons.description: The job to be done and the promise.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

State the customer job and the value promise in one clear sentence.

lessons.title: Lesson 2.2: Choosing a business model
lessons.description: How you create, deliver and capture value.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Describe how money will flow and what must be true for the model to work.

lessons.title: Lesson 2.3: Competitors and your advantage
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Identify realistic competitors/alternatives and your intended advantage.

lessons.title: Module 2 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 2 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: A value proposition should be:
Vague and clever
*Clear about the customer job and the benefit you deliver
Only about your technology
Hidden from customers
explain: Clarity of benefit.
level: 1

Q: A business model describes:
Only the logo
*How the business creates, delivers and captures value
Only the founding story
Only the product features
explain: Full value cycle.
level: 1

Q: Competitive advantage should be:
Easy for anyone to copy immediately
*Meaningful to customers and hard enough to copy that you can build a position
Only lower price forever
Ignored
explain: Meaningful + defensible enough.
level: 2

Q: Alternatives include:
Only identical companies
*Anything customers currently use to address the same job (including “do nothing”)
Only foreign firms
Only apps
explain: Broad definition of competition.
level: 1

Q: Unit economics roughly means:
Total company revenue only
*Whether each unit of sale contributes positively after direct costs
Only fixed costs
Only marketing spend
explain: Contribution per unit.
level: 2

Q: Channels are:
Only social media
*The paths through which customers discover, buy and receive the offer
Only physical shops
Only word of mouth
explain: Discovery to delivery.
level: 2

Q: A strong early advantage might be:
Secret forever from customers
*Speed, local knowledge, specialised service, or a unique distribution relationship
Only having more money
Ignoring customers
explain: Practical early edges.
level: 1

Q: Revising the idea after customer feedback is:
Failure
*Normal and often necessary
Proof the idea was bad forever
Only for large firms
explain: Learning loops.
level: 1

Q: Capturing value means:
Giving everything away
*Having a way to earn revenue that customers accept
Only donations
Only ads
explain: Sustainable capture.
level: 1

Q: The simplest test of a value proposition is:
Internal debate only
*Whether target customers understand it and care enough to try
Trademark registration
A long white paper
explain: Customer reaction.
level: 1

modules.title: Module 3: Business planning
modules.description: Practical plans for marketing, operations and people.

lessons.title: Lesson 3.1: Parts of a business plan
lessons.description: What belongs in a lean plan.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Outline the sections of a lean plan that a partner or lender would expect.

lessons.title: Lesson 3.2: Marketing and sales plan
lessons.description: How customers will find and buy.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Write a simple go-to-market approach for the first 90 days.

lessons.title: Lesson 3.3: Operations and people
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

List the key operational steps and roles needed to deliver the offer reliably.

lessons.title: Module 3 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 3 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: A lean business plan prioritises:
Length over clarity
*Clarity on problem, solution, customers, model, go-to-market and numbers
Only the founding myth
Secret strategies only
explain: Decision-useful clarity.
level: 1

Q: Go-to-market means:
Ignoring customers
*How you will reach and convert the first customers
Only mass advertising
Only product development
explain: Path to customers.
level: 1

Q: Operations planning should cover:
Only the CEO’s calendar
*Key steps to deliver the product/service consistently
Only marketing slogans
Only fundraising
explain: Delivery reliability.
level: 1

Q: Early sales often rely on:
Only paid ads at scale
*Direct outreach, existing networks and focused channels
Ignoring feedback
Perfect automation only
explain: Hands-on early sales.
level: 2

Q: Roles in a tiny team should be:
Completely undefined
*Clear enough that critical work is owned
Only titles with no tasks
Rotated daily randomly
explain: Ownership of critical work.
level: 2

Q: A 90-day plan is useful because:
It replaces all strategy
*It forces concrete near-term actions and learning goals
It is required by law
It avoids all numbers
explain: Near-term concreteness.
level: 1

Q: Assumptions in a plan should be:
Hidden
*Listed so they can be tested
Treated as facts forever
Only financial
explain: Testable assumptions.
level: 2

Q: Customer acquisition cost matters because:
It is always zero
*It must be recoverable through the value of a customer relationship
Only large companies track it
It replaces product quality
explain: Sustainability of growth.
level: 2

Q: Quality and reliability in operations affect:
Only internal pride
*Customer retention and word of mouth
Nothing external
Only suppliers
explain: Delivery quality drives growth.
level: 1

Q: The plan is a tool for:
Filing and forgetting
*Aligning action, raising resources and updating as you learn
Avoiding customers
Proving you never change
explain: Living tool.
level: 1

lessons.title: Lesson 4.1: Startup costs and funding
lessons.description: What you need before and after launch.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

List one-time and recurring costs and realistic funding sources for the first stage.

lessons.title: Lesson 4.2: Pricing and break-even
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Set a price hypothesis and estimate break-even volume.

lessons.title: Lesson 4.3: Simple cash flow forecasts
lessons.description: Cash in and cash out over time.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Build a simple monthly cash forecast for the first six months.

lessons.title: Module 4 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 4 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: Startup costs include:
Only the founder’s time forever
*One-time setup costs and ongoing operating costs
Only marketing
Only taxes
explain: Setup + operating.
level: 1

Q: Break-even is the point at which:
Cash is infinite
*Contribution covers fixed costs (profit ≈ 0)
All loans are repaid
Marketing stops
explain: Zero-profit threshold.
level: 1

Q: Cash flow differs from profit because:
They are identical
*Timing of receipts and payments can create cash shortfalls even when profitable on paper
Cash never matters
Profit ignores all costs
explain: Timing matters.
level: 2

Q: Pricing should consider:
Only competitors’ prices
*Costs, customer willingness to pay, and positioning
Only costs
Only gut feel
explain: Multiple inputs.
level: 1

Q: A simple cash forecast helps:
Avoid all planning
*Anticipate shortfalls and plan funding or cost cuts
Replace sales
Ignore suppliers
explain: Foresight.
level: 1

Q: Funding sources for early stages often include:
Only large venture funds
*Personal savings, friends/family, grants, revenue, and carefully chosen debt
Only IPOs
Only government ownership
explain: Realistic early sources.
level: 2

Q: Underpricing to “get customers” can:
Always build a healthy business
*Create a business that cannot cover costs or invest in quality
Eliminate competition forever
Increase margins automatically
explain: Unsustainable prices hurt.
level: 2

Q: Fixed costs are:
Zero for all startups
*Costs that do not change much with small changes in volume
Only materials
Only wages of temporary staff
explain: Volume-insensitive costs.
level: 1

Q: Variable costs change with:
The weather only
*The volume of sales or production
Only the founder’s mood
Nothing
explain: Volume-linked costs.
level: 1

Q: The financial plan should be updated when:
Never
*Significant assumptions change or new information arrives
Only at year end
Only if profitable
explain: Living numbers.
level: 2

modules.title: Module 5: Enterprise development
modules.description: Launch, risk and leadership of a small business.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.1: Launching and growing
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Define launch milestones and early growth experiments.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.2: Managing risk
lessons.description: Identify and reduce the biggest threats.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

List top risks and one practical mitigation for each.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.3: Leadership of a small business
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Describe leadership habits that keep a small team effective and honest.

lessons.title: Module 5 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 5 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: Launch milestones should be:
Vague aspirations
*Observable events that show the business is working (first paid customer, repeat purchase, etc.)
Only internal feelings
Only social media likes
explain: Observable progress.
level: 1

Q: Risk management starts with:
Ignoring risks
*Identifying the biggest risks and reducing them where practical
Buying every insurance product
Avoiding all action
explain: Identify then mitigate.
level: 1

Q: Early growth experiments test:
Nothing
*Channels, offers and processes to find what scales efficiently
Only the logo colour
Only hiring plans
explain: Learn what works.
level: 1

Q: Small-business leadership requires:
Avoiding all hard conversations
*Clear decisions, honest communication and continuous learning
Only charisma
Only technical skill
explain: Decisions + honesty + learning.
level: 2

Q: Customer retention often matters more than:
All acquisition forever
*Constant acquisition of one-time buyers who never return
Product quality
Pricing
explain: Retention compounds.
level: 2

Q: A practical risk mitigation might be:
Hoping for the best only
*Diversifying suppliers, keeping a cash buffer, or validating demand before big inventory buys
Ignoring insurance entirely always
Sharing all passwords
explain: Concrete reductions.
level: 1

Q: Culture in a tiny team is shaped mostly by:
Posters
*What leaders do and tolerate daily
Only written policies
Customer complaints only
explain: Behaviour sets culture.
level: 2

Q: Learning systems (reviews, metrics, customer feedback) help:
Freeze the business
*Improve decisions as the environment changes
Replace all strategy
Avoid all change
explain: Adaptation.
level: 1

Q: Scaling too early can:
Always be safe
*Amplify broken processes and burn cash
Fix product problems automatically
Eliminate competition
explain: Scale amplifies what exists.
level: 2

Q: The entrepreneurial journey is best treated as:
A single brilliant idea
*A series of experiments, sales, operations and learning loops
Avoiding all customers
Only fundraising
explain: Iterative practice.
level: 1
